metadata.selection_layer: raw candidate head; runtime confidence/support gates are not evaluated

protocol.memory: 20 shuffled historical environment-labelled records; both observed actions for every code; only 5 alpha-positive and 5 beta-positive bindings in every rulebook
protocol.pair_balance: same query state and executed action, complementary binding map and opposite observed return; no deterministic state-only candidate ranking can exceed 0.5 over pairs
protocol.training_labels: one executed action's observed +/-3 reward per current decision; no unexecuted candidate label is passed to train_model
protocol.temporal_boundary: all memory observations and settlements precede the decision, current settlement follows it; evaluation decision timestamps follow training examples
protocol.split: disjoint complete mapping assignments and episode/experience IDs; vocabulary is shared; evaluation targets never select training hyperparameters
protocol.evaluation_controls: empty_memory removes all evidence; complemented_rulebook replaces the evidence by the paired inverse mapping while retaining original targets to probe dependence on bindings

datasets.heldout_unit: complete binding assignment and episode; code vocabulary is shared
datasets.label_policy: train_model receives one executed action and its +/-3 observed return; both-candidate ground truth exists only in evaluation metadata

limitations: Synthetic memory binding task, not a remote LLM, real Agent or real-user performance result.
Small CPU models, limited updates and two default seeds do not establish a statistically reliable superiority claim.
Ranking ground truth for both candidates is generated by the synthetic environment and used only for evaluation, never training.
Learner also predicts PRE return without knowing the randomly executed action; its auxiliary target has irreducible conditional noise on this task.
Empty/inverted-memory evaluation is a diagnostic distribution shift, not a causal intervention estimate for a deployed Agent.
Training timings include encoding, private model copy, optimizer, objective evaluations and updates; machine load and backend execution order affect latency.
